requirements.text: If the problem exists, link the critical incident INC0000006 to this problem record
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_006' AND problem = 'PRB_001' AND status = 'in_progress' AND org_id = 'ORG_001' AND service = 'SVC_001' AND category IN ('software', 'network')
assumptions: INC0000006 is INC_006 (Critical system outage, Email Service SVC_001, ORG_001, critical, in progress), the only Email Service incident created 20-24 February 2024 that is in progress; INC_019 shares the number but belongs to ORG_002 and SVC_003
PRB_001 (Intermittent email service outages, SVC_001, ORG_001) exists, so the condition for linking holds
status stays in_progress: the request calls it the current status and asks for no change; kept from the benchmark check
service and category kept from the benchmark scope check, whose date window on created_at is dropped; both hold for INC_006 on the seed

disagreement: cells: A adds service = 'SVC_001' and category IN ('software', 'network'), B tests problem, status and org_id only; chose A's because both are right and A's is tighter, carrying the scope check's filters on the one row it counts

requirements.text: This incident has impact and priority already set to high/critical levels
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_006' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical' AND org_id = 'ORG_001'
assumptions: the request states impact and priority are already set, so linking the problem must not alter them
urgency kept from the benchmark check; high impact and high urgency give critical in the policy matrix

requirements.text: Create a knowledge article documenting the critical email service outage, including the complete system outage symptoms, current investigation steps (server restart, database corruption investigation), and the webmail workaround
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM knowledge WHERE knowledge_id = 'KB_006' AND (title LIKE '%Email%Service%' OR title LIKE '%email%outage%') AND body LIKE '%outage%' AND body LIKE '%restart%' AND body LIKE '%corrupt%' AND body LIKE '%webmail%' AND state = 'published' AND owner_id = 'USER_002' AND org_id = 'ORG_001'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (KB_006 after KB_005); the task creates one article
title kept from the benchmark check as two alternatives: either pattern satisfies it (the sql joins them with OR); not fixed by request or policy
body must name the outage symptoms, the server restart, the database corruption investigation and the webmail workaround, as the request lists them; all four body patterns must match
state published kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy
owner is the acting user, Priya Sharma (USER_002), who writes the article; org ORG_001 is hers and the incident's

disagreement: body: A LIKE '%corrupt%', B LIKE '%corruption%'; chose '%corrupt%' because it accepts every form of the request's word ('corrupted database' as well as 'database corruption'), while '%corruption%' would fail a faithful article worded the other way

requirements.text: Link this knowledge article to the incident INC0000006 as 'suggested' for agent reference
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_knowledge WHERE incident_kb_id = 'IKB_006' AND incident_id = 'INC_006' AND knowledge_id = 'KB_006' AND used_as = 'suggested' AND org_id = 'ORG_001'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (IKB_006 after IKB_005); the task creates one link
'this knowledge article' is the one just created, KB_006; the benchmark check leaves the article open

requirements.text: Send an alert notification to Marcus Thompson (marcus.thompson@techcorp.com) with a summary
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_008' AND incident_id = 'INC_006' AND email = 'marcus.thompson@techcorp.com' AND type = 'alert' AND org_id = 'ORG_001' AND (subject LIKE '%Email Service%' OR subject LIKE '%INC0000006%') AND message LIKE '%INC%006%' AND message LIKE '%outage%' AND message LIKE '%SLA%' AND message LIKE '%PRB%001%' AND message LIKE '%Service Desk%' AND message LIKE '%KB%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_008 after NOTIF_007); the task creates one notification
Marcus Thompson is USER_001, whose email the request gives; the notification refers to INC_006, the incident the summary is about
type alert: the request asks for an alert notification
subject kept from the benchmark check as two alternatives: either pattern satisfies it (the sql joins them with OR); not fixed by request or policy

the message must carry each part of the summary the request lists (all six patterns must match): the incident (INC0000006 or INC_006), the outage, the SLA status, the problem (PRB_001 or PRB0000001), the assigned group and the article's reference
the article's reference is its id (KB_006) or number (KB0000006), both of which contain KB

disagreement: message incident and problem patterns: A '%INC%006%' and '%PRB%001%', B '%INC0000006%' and '%PRB_001%'; chose A's because the request mixes ids and numbers, so either form names the record, and B's would fail a summary that names INC_006 or PRB0000001

disagreement: message group pattern: A '%Service Desk%', B '%GROUP_002%'; chose '%Service Desk%' because the request names the group 'GROUP_002 Service Desk' and its seed name is Service Desk Operations, so a readable summary carries the name whether or not it adds the id

disagreement: message outage and article patterns: A tests '%outage%' and '%KB%', B neither; kept both because the request lists the outage in the incident details and the article reference among the summary's parts

requirements.text: Identify the single critical incident for Email Service between February 20-24, 2024 that is currently in 'In Progress' status (INC0000006)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id IN ('INC_014', 'INC_019') AND problem IS NULL
assumptions: INC_019 shares the number INC0000006 (Email attachment size limit, ORG_002, SVC_003) and INC_014 is the other open Email Service incident opened in the window (Monitor display flickering, new); neither is the single critical incident, so neither is linked to a problem

disagreement: selector and cells: A every Email Service incident other than INC_001 and INC_006 with problem = 'PRB_001' (expected 0, carrying the scope check), B INC_014 and INC_019 with problem IS NULL (expected 2, new); chose B's because INC_004 and INC_007 are child incidents of INC_006 that the policy's rule (a problem links all affected incidents) may require linking, so they cannot be forbidden, while INC_019 is the row a lookup by number would sweep in; the rows lie outside the scope check's filters, so the requirement is new

verify_only_critical_incident_in_scope.evidence: its DATE(created_at) window tests a server-kept column, which no step writes and no requirement can carry as a cell; INC_006 was created 2024-02-21 08:05, inside the window, and on the seed it is the only Email Service incident that meets the check's other filters, so the window is dropped and the rest (service, category, status, problem, org) is carried on INC_006

notes:
disagreement: value: the problem link's cells: one pass adds service = 'SVC_001' and category IN ('software', 'network') from the scope check, the other does not; chose the tighter form, since both cells hold for INC_006 and carry the scope check once its date window is dropped.
disagreement: value: the article body's corruption pattern: one pass '%corrupt%', the other '%corruption%'; chose '%corrupt%', which accepts any wording of the request's 'database corruption'.
disagreement: value: the notification message's incident and problem patterns: one pass accepts id or number ('%INC%006%', '%PRB%001%'), the other only the quoted forms ('%INC0000006%', '%PRB_001%'); chose id or number because the request mixes the two forms.
disagreement: value: the notification message's group pattern: one pass the name ('%Service Desk%'), the other the id ('%GROUP_002%'); chose the name, which the request and the seed (Service Desk Operations) share.
disagreement: value: the notification message's outage and article patterns: one pass tests '%outage%' and '%KB%', the other neither; kept both because the request lists the outage and the article reference as parts of the summary.
disagreement: value: the boundary stay: one pass every other Email Service incident except INC_001 with no PRB_001 link (expected 0, carrying the scope check), the other INC_014 and INC_019 with no problem at all (expected 2, new); chose the second because INC_001, INC_004 and INC_007 are child incidents of INC_006 that the policy's linking rule may cover, while INC_019 shares the number INC0000006.
disagreement: disposition of verify_only_critical_incident_in_scope: one pass repaired (date window on created_at dropped), the other kept; chose repaired because a server-kept created_at cannot be a cell, so the requirement that carries the check drops that predicate.
INC_006 has no incident_sla rows, so the SLA check finds nothing and nothing is breaching; the policy's breach escalation does not apply and the notification's SLA status can only say so. PRB_002 shares the number PRB0000001 with PRB_001 but belongs to ORG_002; the request names PRB_001 by id.
PRB_001 already holds the webmail workaround. The policy's rule that a workaround be published to linked incidents and relevant articles belongs to the step that records a workaround, which this request does not take; the request places the workaround in the new article, and no tool updates problems, so no further requirement is drawn from it.
INC_001, INC_004 and INC_007 are child incidents of INC_006; whether they may also be linked to PRB_001 is not tested either way.
The article's contents are tested in body; an article that puts them only in short_description would fail. Knowledge visibility and notification status are not fixed by the request or the policy and are not tested. The impact and priority check holds before the agent acts, so it is weak; it is carried as a stay. The acting user, Priya Sharma, holds the manager role, with full rights on incidents and knowledge.
